metaTitle: Homepage Revamp — Adda247 | Designit Case Study
metaDescription: Revamping the Adda247 home screen to improve onboarding, boost engagement and drive free-to-paid conversion for 3M+ competitive exam students.
author: Designit
summary: Revamping the Adda247 home screen to enhance onboarding, boost engagement, and drive free-to-paid conversion for 3M+ competitive exam students.

hero.alt: Two phones showing the redesigned Adda247 home screen with study material, quizzes and educator content

overview.label: Project Overview
overview.heading: A smarter home for India's biggest EdTech
paras: The Adda247 app serves millions of students preparing for competitive exams. However, its home screen felt outdated and failed to guide users effectively — leading to low retention and drop-off at a critical stage.

This project focused on revamping the home section to deliver a structured, frictionless onboarding flow for new users and a personalised, high-engagement experience for existing ones — while nudging free users toward paid conversion.

metaCards: UX Research · Information Architecture · UI Design · Prototyping · Handoff

challenges.label: Business Challenges
challenges.heading: Four problems to solve
intro: The platform had high engagement potential but was actively undermining its own retention and conversion goals.

items.title: Outdated UI
items.body: The home section lacked modern design aesthetics, making it less appealing and trustworthy — especially to first-time users evaluating whether to invest time in the platform.

items.title: High Drop-off Rates
items.body: Many new users abandoned the app immediately due to a poor onboarding experience. There were no guided entry points to communicate value before redirecting users to the store.

items.title: Lack of Product Discovery
items.body: Users struggled to navigate and understand the app's value proposition. High-click features like Quizzes and Job Alerts were buried — causing users to miss the most engaging content.

items.title: Retention Issues
items.body: Engaged users did not find enough reasons to return consistently. The home feed was cluttered with competing content types, banner ads, and cognitive overload that discouraged daily use.

problemStatement: How might we create a seamless and engaging home experience that fosters trust, enhances product discovery, and motivates students to study — while reducing clutter, improving navigation, and leveraging top educators to drive retention and conversions?

approach.label: Our Process
approach.heading: How we approached it
intro: A structured four-phase design process grounded in user behaviour data and iterative validation.

steps.title: Research & Opportunity Areas
steps.body: Behavioural analysis of 3M+ user interactions, heatmaps, session recordings, and stakeholder interviews to identify the biggest friction points and missed engagement opportunities.

steps.title: What & How
steps.body: Synthesised research into a clear problem statement, user persona (Yash — a first-time free user preparing for defence exams), and a structured information architecture for the new home experience.

steps.title: Feedback, UX Patterns & Consistency
steps.body: Explored multiple layout concepts around three content buckets — Watch, Practice, Read. Validated patterns against competitive benchmarks and Adda247's own highest-performing content types.

steps.title: Mockups, High-fidelity & Prototype Delivery
steps.body: Iterated through multiple design rounds, built interactive prototypes for user validation, and delivered production-ready Figma files with full component documentation and developer handoff specs.

decisions.label: Design Decisions
decisions.heading: What we redesigned
intro: Five structural changes that transformed the home screen from a cluttered feed into a high-conversion learning hub.

items.title: Unified Home Experience
items.body: Replaced the scattered Feed & Study Material dual-tab structure with a single, cohesive home screen organised around user intent: Watch, Practice, Read.

items.title: Improved Navigation
items.body: Reduced reliance on the hamburger menu by surfacing key sections directly in the bottom nav and home screen. Teacher-based navigation was elevated per user preference data.

items.title: Data-Driven Feature Placement
items.body: High-traffic content — Quizzes (1.47M clicks), Job Alerts, Study Materials, Current Affairs — was promoted to above-the-fold positions with visual hierarchy matching actual usage.

items.title: Engagement Boosters
items.body: Added daily streaks, badges, personalised educator recommendations, and community nudges to create sustainable return loops and build emotional connection with the platform.

items.title: Optimised Premium Visibility
items.body: Premium content and trial offers were repositioned with clear value framing — ensuring new users experienced product value before being redirected to purchase, reducing early drop-off.

items.title: Structured Onboarding Flow
items.body: New users now receive a guided, frictionless entry experience that showcases the app's core value proposition through self-trial flows before any premium upsell prompt.

results.label: Conclusion
results.heading: Impact of the redesign
intro: The new design streamlined navigation, improved content discoverability, and prioritised high-engagement features — delivering a more intuitive, personalised learning journey.

empathy.heading: Who we designed for
empathy.intro: Most people who open the Adda247 app are deciding, quickly, whether it is worth their limited study time. The home screen has a few seconds to answer that.

people.context: Often preparing for a government or defence exam, exploring before paying. They need to see value before they see a price.
Already studying, looking for today's quiz, current affairs or the class they bought. They need the next useful thing within reach.
Needs engagement to turn into trust, and trust into paid plans, without banner ads crowding out the learning.

painPoints: The most-used content, study material, sat behind extra navigation steps.
Daily Quiz, a top feature, was visually deprioritised on the screen.
Video and community features were buried, so few people found them.
Heavy hamburger-menu use signalled that the home screen was not answering the question 'where do I go next?'.

faq.q: What is Keeping ADDA Home Simple & Approachable?
faq.a: Revamping the Adda247 home screen to enhance onboarding, boost engagement, and drive free-to-paid conversion for 3M+ competitive exam students.

faq.q: What problem did Keeping ADDA Home Simple & Approachable solve?
faq.a: The home section lacked modern design aesthetics, making it less appealing and trustworthy — especially to first-time users evaluating whether to invest time in the platform. The question we set out to answer: How might we create a seamless and engaging home experience that fosters trust, enhances product discovery, and motivates students to study — while reducing clutter, improving navigation, and leveraging top educators to drive retention and conversions?

faq.q: How did Designit approach Keeping ADDA Home Simple & Approachable?
faq.a: We worked in 4 phases: Research & Opportunity Areas; what & how; feedback, ux patterns & consistency; mockups, high-fidelity & prototype delivery. Behavioural analysis of 3M+ user interactions, heatmaps, session recordings, and stakeholder interviews to identify the biggest friction points and missed engagement opportunities..

faq.q: What should an EdTech app's home screen show first?
faq.a: What the learner came for, in the order they use it. For Adda247 that meant organising the home around three intents, Watch, Practice and Read, and promoting the most-used content (study material, Daily Quiz, Job Alerts, Current Affairs) above the fold, ahead of promotions.

faq.q: How do you improve free-to-paid conversion without hurting engagement?
faq.a: Let people experience value before the upsell. The redesigned home gives new users a guided self-trial of the core features and frames premium content by what it adds, instead of redirecting them to the store on first open.

faq.q: Why does heavy hamburger-menu use matter?
faq.a: It usually means the screen in front of people is not giving them a clear next step. On Adda247, menu taps were one of the signals that key sections needed to move into the bottom navigation and the home screen itself.

faq.q: How do you decide what goes above the fold?
faq.a: Usage data first, opinion second. We ranked features by how often learners actually used them and gave the visual hierarchy to match, so the most valuable actions are visible without scrolling.

faq.q: What are engagement boosters in a learning app?
faq.a: Small, honest reasons to come back: daily streaks, badges, educator recommendations and community nudges. They work when they reward real study, not just opening the app.

faq.q: Who was the persona for the Adda247 home redesign?
faq.a: Yash, a 17-year-old first-time free user from a tier 2 city preparing for defence exams. He wants quality material, a free trial or an affordable plan, progress tracking and doubt resolution, and he struggles with too much choice and with convincing his parents to pay for a course.

faq.q: What did the Adda247 user journey map show?
faq.a: The lowest moments came when students compared apps, checked prices, chose a course and made their first practice attempts. The redesign focused there: value before the store, clearer course information, and practice that is easy to start from the home screen.

context.label: Background
context.heading: Setting up the context
paras: The platform serves students and professionals who want quick access to study material, quizzes and career-related content. Navigation problems, cognitive overload and poor content prioritisation were getting in the way of all three.

Engagement potential was high, but the home screen was not keeping people. Fixing the experience could improve discoverability and retention, and lead to better learning outcomes: a home that feels more intuitive, more engaging and easier to come back to.

The brief was to revamp the home section so that new users get a structured, frictionless onboarding, existing users get a personalised and engaging experience, the interface builds trust with modern UI, and free users are nudged towards paid plans through self-trial.
list: Motivate users to explore and engage with the app.
Enable self-trial for new and existing students, to drive product-led growth.
Establish trust through a clean, modern interface.
Nudge users towards paid plans, improving conversion.

userChallenges.label: Problem areas
userChallenges.heading: Where the old home screen got in the way
intro: We audited the existing app screen by screen and grouped what we found into four problem areas.

groups.title: Navigation and discovery
items: Dual-tab confusion
Feed and Study Material as two tabs split attention and hid content.
Ineffective navigation
375K users relied on the hamburger menu, a sign that key sections were hard to find.
Teacher-based navigation
Students prefer to reach material through specific teachers, but the app did not emphasise them.

img.alt: The old Adda247 app with separate Feed and Study Material tabs
img.caption: Before: Feed and Study Material as separate tabs.

groups.title: Content accessibility and engagement
items: Poor prioritisation
High-click features (study material, quizzes, job alerts) were not visually prioritised; Daily Quiz was under-emphasised despite 1.47M clicks.
Hidden premium content
Premium content, used by 110K+ unique users, was buried in lists.
Study material
Long, unstructured lists made content hard to find, and similar icons made navigation unintuitive.

groups.title: Cognitive overload
items: Information overload
A cluttered home and long articles raised cognitive strain; the feed was built for engagement but did not retain people.
Feed issues
Most users scrolled only 3–5 times, competing content types fought for attention, and banner ads broke the flow.

img.alt: The old Adda247 feed with a promotional banner covering the content
img.caption: Before: banner ads interrupting the feed.

groups.title: Barriers to learning
items: Feature access
Power Capsules (45K users) sat at the bottom of a list; videos had low engagement (57K users) yet appeared in several places; Current Affairs was placed twice.
Buried material
60% of study materials lived in separate sections, which made them hard to reach.
Onboarding
New users were sent to the store too soon, before they had seen the product's value.
